Query Trino as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__trino.R
oauth_db_trino.Rd

Query data through Trino or Starburst Enterprise with each visitor's account and cluster permissions. The RTrino connection supports DBI and dbplyr. A catalog selects the data source; a schema selects a group of tables within it.

Usage

oauth_db_trino(
  authorization,
  host,
  catalog,
  schema,
  user,
  ...,
  port = NULL,
  ca_bundle = NULL,
  target = NULL,
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

Function providing the visitor's current sign-in authorization. Pass auth$connection from shinyOAuth without parentheses. To select a saved account, use a function calling auth$connection(id).

host

Cluster hostname or HTTPS origin.

catalog, schema

Default Trino catalog and schema.

user

Trino username, or a function returning it for the selected account. Use a reactive function when the username can change.

...

RTrino connection options, such as timeout, bigint, query_max_run_time, or extra.headers.

port

HTTPS port. NULL uses the port in host, or 443.

ca_bundle

Optional CA certificate bundle path for RTrino.

target

Name of the service token to use in your shinyOAuth client. Named targets let one sign-in obtain tokens for different services. NULL uses the client's default token.

required_scopes

Additional OAuth permissions to check before use. Request them on the shinyOAuth client first; this check doesn't request consent or grant database privileges.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

session

The visitor's Shiny session. Usually inferred when you create the helper inside server().

Value

A reactive function, usually named con. Call connection <- con() inside a render or reactive expression, then pass the connection to DBI. Before sign-in, the function waits quietly.

Details

Install RTrino 0.1.0 or later. Create the helper inside server() and call con() inside a render or reactive expression before querying.

Sign-in settings

Configure a shinyOAuth client for the cluster's trusted provider and audience. Set user to match the cluster's identity mapping; the server checks that the visitor can use that username.

Connection lifetime

RTrino gets a current token for each request, including result pages. Token renewal preserves the connection. Account or username changes replace it; sign-out and session end close it.

See also

vignette("trino", package = "shinyOAuthDB") has sign-in setup and a complete app.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
con <- oauth_db_trino(
  auth$connection,
  host = "https://trino.example.org",
  catalog = "lakehouse",
  schema = "reporting",
  user = function() shiny::req(auth$token@userinfo$email)
)
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  connection <- con()
  DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT * FROM Orders LIMIT 20")
})
} # }
